item.title: World News in Brief: Vaccine crisis in Yemen, aid for Ukraine, another UNRWA staffer killed
item.description: More than 364,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since the beginning of August as fighting and insecurity continue, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said on Tuesday.

item.title: Decades of gains against AIDS could unravel as HIV funding dries up
item.description: Decades of progress against AIDS, one of the greatest public health achievements in history, could go into reverse as international HIV funding is cut and campaigns against human rights and gender equality gain ground, the UN agency devoted to ending the pandemic warned Tuesday in a new report.

item.title: ‘Far too much failure’: UN deputy chief’s final call to end violence against women
item.description: UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed warned on Tuesday that another woman or girl would be killed by a partner or family member before she finished speaking, as she called for justice for survivors and consequences for perpetrators.

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Can conflict resolution keep pace as AI and drones reshape war?
item.description: When the UN was founded in 1945, computers, the internet and satellites were the stuff of science fiction. Today, artificial intelligence (AI) is already assisting in targeting, drones are reshaping warfare and disinformation is spreading in unprecedented ways, fuelling record levels of conflict. The Security Council on Tuesday is weighing these changes, with UN chief António Guterres telling ambassadors, “killer robots must have no place in our future.”

item.title: DR Congo: Concern for trapped Ebola workers as violence against women and girls deepens
item.description: Staff from the World Health Organization (WHO) and Ebola responders remain trapped in a hospital in Ituri province, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), as heavy fighting continues in the vicinity, the UN agency said in an update on Tuesday.

item.title: Colombia: Guterres urges renewed commitment to landmark peace deal
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres has commended Colombia for progress achieved in the decade since a landmark accord known as the Final Peace Agreement ended more than 50 years of insurgency but stressed the need to fully implement its provisions.

item.title: Five women killed every hour by partners or family members
item.description: Some 47,000 women and girls were killed by intimate partners or family members in 2025 – five every hour – according to new UN figures published on Tuesday.
